deterministicChecks.name: tests / unit and contract tests (ubuntu-latest)
deterministicChecks.proves: All 208 repository tests pass, including the 21 service tests that carry AC-1 to AC-10.

deterministicChecks.name: tests / unit and contract tests (windows-latest)
deterministicChecks.proves: The service is cross-platform. The same command runs on both.

deterministicChecks.name: tests / acceptance criteria are all covered
deterministicChecks.proves: Every criterion in SPEC-001 maps to a named test. A criterion without a test fails here.

deterministicChecks.name: content-validation / documents and prepared artefacts
deterministicChecks.proves: Links, anchors, duplicate ids, synthetic-data rules, and the prepared fallback set.

deterministicChecks.name: workflow-security / workflow source rules
deterministicChecks.proves: Every third-party action is pinned to a full commit SHA in both the source and the compiled lock, no workflow uses pull_request_target, every checkout sets persist-credentials: false, no agent job holds a write permission, and the supported lanes exclude engine and MCP credentials from the model sandbox.

deterministicChecks.name: workflow-security / compile agentic workflows and verify lock freshness
deterministicChecks.proves: Each source is recompiled with the pinned compiler and the result is byte-compared with the committed .lock.yml. A source edit that was not recompiled fails here, and so does a hand-edited lock.

deterministicChecks.name: codeql / analyze javascript
deterministicChecks.proves: Static analysis with the security-extended query suite found no alert.

deterministicChecks.name: dependency-review / review dependency changes
deterministicChecks.proves: No dependency was added, so nothing to review. The check still runs so the first one that arrives is reviewed at the pull request.

aiReview.separationRule: An AI review is a reviewer, not a gate. It cannot mark a check green and it cannot approve on behalf of a code owner.

finding.summary: The unavailable branch built its response object by spreading the catalogue item directly, which would have carried the internal block into the payload.
finding.reviewerJudgement: Correct and worth acting on. AC-4 would have caught it, but only after the fact; the reviewer caught it in the diff. Fixed before this pull request was ready to merge.

remediation.commit: fix: project the suggestion through toPublicItem
remediation.diff:
-      suggestion: { ...substitute, siteId, available }
+      suggestion: { ...toPublicItem(substitute), siteId, available: available(siteId, substitute.sku) }
remediation.recheck: tests re-ran and stayed green; AC-4 now proves the boundary rather than assuming it

secretScanning.note: Push protection blocks a recognised secret at the push, before it reaches history. Availability depends on the plan and on repository settings, so this repository explains the control rather than staging a fake block.
secretScanning.capabilityFallback: If push protection is not enabled on the demonstration repository, say so and show the setting instead of implying a block occurred.

mdash.stageSourceQuote: Codename MDASH - Agentic code scanner initiative (private preview)
mdash.stageSourceNote: The overview page describes the capability but does not carry the stage. The initiative page's own title does, so the stage is cited from there and quoted rather than paraphrased.
mdash.positioning: A Microsoft agentic code scanner in the Defender and Exposure Management family. It runs a multi-agent source-scanning pipeline and publishes its findings into Exposure Management.
mdash.relationToCodeQL: It overlaps and complements CodeQL as a code scanner. It is not runtime or exposure context, and it does not replace static analysis. Nothing in this repository depends on it.
mdash.claimBoundary: Named as a private preview capability with its stage stated. No screenshot, no simulated finding, no claim that it ran here.

credentialBoundary.supportedLanes: The agent job holds read-only GitHub permissions, and the compiled lock passes --exclude-env for five named variables, so none of them is present in the model sandbox. Both supported locks also set GH_AW_INFO_FIREWALL_ENABLED to true.

excludedFromAgentSandbox.name: COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN
excludedFromAgentSandbox.why: the token the Copilot engine authenticates with

excludedFromAgentSandbox.name: GITHUB_MCP_SERVER_TOKEN
excludedFromAgentSandbox.why: the token the GitHub MCP server authenticates with

excludedFromAgentSandbox.name: MCP_GATEWAY_API_KEY
excludedFromAgentSandbox.why: the key the MCP gateway authenticates with

excludedFromAgentSandbox.name: ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_TOKEN
excludedFromAgentSandbox.why: not a credential itself; with the URL below it is what a job uses to mint a federated OIDC token

excludedFromAgentSandbox.name: ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_URL
excludedFromAgentSandbox.why: not a credential itself; the endpoint the request token is presented to

credentialBoundary.threatDetectionSandbox: The threat-detection job excludes the three of those five that exist in its environment: COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN, ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_TOKEN and ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_URL. The two MCP credentials are never present there, so they are not on its list.
credentialBoundary.experimentalException: The OpenCode sample lock maps OPENAI_API_KEY to the COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN secret and does not exclude that variable, so the Copilot token reaches the model sandbox under another name. It also sets GH_AW_INFO_FIREWALL_ENABLED to false. Both differences are material, and both are why that lane is prepared evidence rather than a live control path.
credentialBoundary.wording: Never say the agent job holds no secret. Say what is true: read-only GitHub permissions, and five named variables excluded from the model sandbox — three engine or MCP credentials, and the two OIDC request variables that would let the job mint a federated token.

authority.codeowners: .github/CODEOWNERS requires an owner review on app/src/catalog.js, app/src/substitution.js, docs/spec/, and the workflow definitions.
authority.ruleset: A repository ruleset on main requires a pull request, requires the deterministic checks above, requires a code-owner review, and blocks force pushes.
authority.humanApproval: One named person approved. The approval is attributed, dated, and attached to a specific commit SHA.
authority.whyItMatters: Every automated actor in this loop is read-only. The only write to main goes through an accountable human decision.

verifiableClaims: The merge could not happen until the required checks were green.
The AI review could not satisfy the code-owner requirement.
The approval is attributed to a person and to a commit.
